reasons: Classification is correct: Article XII is a one-way Licensee-to-Licensor indemnity with no Licensor IP indemnity anywhere, which the rule expressly identifies as walk-away territory, so it fails both the preferred and fallback positions.

The redline follows the rule's own redline guidance for one-sided clauses — it adds the Licensor defence/indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics, and narrows the Licensee indemnity to licence-restriction breach, our breach of law and content we supply, matching the preferred position's limits on Customer indemnity.

The failed changed-character-ratio checks are expected here: reversing a wholly one-sided indemnity and inserting a new Vendor obligation cannot be done with a smaller edit, and no unrelated terms were disturbed (only 'solely' and the over-broad Licensee triggers were touched).

Carving the Licensor indemnity out of the Article XIII cap is substantively necessary because Article XIII otherwise disclaims Licensor liability for infringement, and the comment appropriately offers the fallback (usual IP-indemnity exclusions plus a super-cap) as a negotiating alternative.

Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the required prefix, explains the change and the playbook basis, and correctly defers the cap level itself to the limitation-of-liability rule (no double-flagging).
